records.title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells
records.summary:
Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03350-7

RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale. Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

records.title: Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing
records.summary:
Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03358-z

ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins. By using human AGO2 instead of bacterial CRISPR–Cas proteins, ALTER mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications while also proving generally more effective than dCas13-based editors.

records.title: Translating base editors: a decade of progress from the bench to the clinic
records.summary:
Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41573-026-01548-7

Base editing, a gene editing technology capable of installing point mutations with high efficiency and precision, was first reported a decade ago. This Review examines the evolution of base editors and their road to clinical translation, highlighting key advances, ongoing challenges and the current clinical trial landscape.

records.title: Next-generation immune cell engagers for B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases
records.summary:
Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41573-026-01534-z

Immune cell engagers are emerging as a strategy for deep B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases. This Review examines their mechanisms, clinical development and next-generation designs, including T cell, natural killer cell and γδ T cell-engaging formats, and considers lessons from haematological malignancies to improve efficacy, safety and durability of immune modulation.
